checklist: Verify your contractor license is current and valid in MO
Confirm your liability insurance is active (certificate is conditional only when the listed condition applies at permit office)
Have the property address and legal parcel number ready
Know the project value/cost — required on most permit applications

Confirm the required license is active and matches the application: Commercial contractor pulls the permit on behalf of the owner; the contractor's license and registration information must appear on the application. For the gas dryer and plumbing portions, a licensed plumbing/gas contractor should be listed for that scope. For the 600 amp service, a licensed electrical contractor should be listed. The permit is still required for the project even when a licensed contractor submits it.
Bring 2 copies of all documents to Kansas City City Planning & Development
response_body.city_contractor_registration: Kansas City requires local contractor registration/authorization for permit work in many cases. Verify the contractor's current city registration status before submitting the application, because an expired or lapsed city registration can block the permit. Renewal frequency and exact registration workflow were not confirmed in the current source context and should be verified with Kansas City City Planning & Development.

common_mistakes: Submitting the project as a simple trade replacement instead of a commercial change-of-use tenant improvement — that will get bounced because retail-to-laundromat is a use change with multiple code disciplines
Under-sizing or omitting the electrical load calculation for the 600 amp service — laundromat equipment loads are heavy and reviewers will flag missing demand calculations
Forgetting that gas dryers need both gas piping review and venting/exhaust review, not just a mechanical note
Leaving out floor drain details, trap primers, or sanitary routing — plumbing review will not pass without a complete drainage plan

Submitting permit application without verifying current contractor registration status — an expired or lapsed city registration will block your application silently. Verify your registration is current BEFORE submitting.

pro_tips: Kansas City bundles building and trade permits into one valuation-based fee, so submit one complete commercial package instead of trying to split the scope into separate permits.
Put the 600 amp service load calc, RTU cut sheet, and gas dryer venting details in the first plan submittal — that cuts down on correction cycles.
Check your Kansas City contractor registration renewal date before starting any permit application — registration lapses are the #1 avoidable rejection reason.

If the laundromat will have any water heating or backflow-related equipment, show the plumbing fixture schedule and backflow protection on the first submittal so plumbing review does not stall the whole permit.

response_body.zoning_hoa_flag: Commercial laundromat conversions can trigger zoning review for change of use, parking, accessibility, signage, and any exterior equipment or vent penetrations. If the building is in a historic district or overlay, exterior RTU placement, roof penetrations, and signage may need additional approval. HOA restrictions are usually not the issue for commercial property, but lease and site-control restrictions can still delay work.
